sections.heading: The media
sections.body: *los medios de comunicación* (the media), *la prensa* (the press), *el periódico / el diario* (newspaper), *la revista* (magazine), *el noticiero / las noticias* (the news broadcast), *el titular* (headline), *el artículo*, *el / la periodista*, *la entrevista*, *el reportaje* (report / feature), *la red social* (social network), *la noticia falsa* (fake news), *en vivo / en directo* (live).

sections.heading: The passive with ser
sections.body:
The true passive is *ser* + past participle (+ *por* + agent). The participle agrees with the subject:

*El puente fue construido en 1990.* (The bridge was built in 1990.)
*Las leyes son aprobadas por el Congreso.* (Laws are passed by Congress.)
*El ladrón fue detenido por la policía.* (The thief was arrested by the police.)

It's typical of **news and formal writing**. In conversation, Spanish prefers the active voice (*La policía detuvo al ladrón*) or passive *se* (*Se construyó el puente en 1990*).

sections.heading: Headline style
sections.body: Headlines often drop articles and verbs, and use the present for past events: *Detienen a dos hombres por robo en el centro* (Two men arrested for robbery downtown). *Aprobada la nueva ley de educación.* Notice the impersonal third-person plural (*detienen*) — "they" meaning the authorities.
